newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND UPHOLDS LARGE WARNINGS ON CIGARETTE PACKS.
newsitem.headline: POLAND UPHOLDS LARGE WARNINGS ON CIGARETTE PACKS.

text.p: Poland's parliament on Friday voted to retain new rules forcing cigarette packs to carry much larger health warnings than in other European countries, despite arguments this would harm the local tobacco industry.

Lower house deputies voted by 148 to 122 with 100 abstentions against a bid to scrap the big warnings, which are to become compulsory at the end of the year under a 1995 law on limiting the health damage caused by tobacco.
All cigarettes sold in Poland will have have to carry stark warnings over at least 30 percent of each large side of a pack.
But some deputies introduced an amendment aimed at removing this aspect of the new law even before it took effect.

They argued that as Poland's European Union neighbours such as Germany require only a much smaller message covering four percent, foreign products will have an advantage over local ones, especially when Poland joins the EU after the year 2000.
They said Poland should introduce the same size warnings as in the European Union.

Advocates of the new larger messages alleged that the attempted amendment was the result of intense lobbying by domestic and foreign tobacco firms, who feared Poland's tough example would be copied in other European states.

"Our law on health warnings is a precedent in Europe and if it is not changed it could quickly spread to other European states," anti-smoking crusader and cancer specialist Witold Zatonski told a news conference this week.
The 1995 law also introduced restrictions on tobacco advertising but stopped short of a total ban.

Poles are among the world's heaviest smokers and the tobacco industry, privatised last year, has attracted strong foreign investment, but health campaigns and rising duties on tobacco have brought a drop in demand.
Last year about 90 billion cigarettes were sold in Poland, down from 96 billion the previous year.
